Article Title: 'Was she menstruating?' TVK minister's absence from Vijay's UK trip invites sexist remarks from DMK
Article Text:
Sexist remarks over Keerthana’s London absence trigger political row

thangai

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu industries minister S Keerthana was subjected to sexist remarks by DMK which was questioning her absence from chief minister C Joseph Vijay’s recent London visit. The remarks by DMK leader Vaishnavi has triggered a political controversy.Vijay travelled to London to flag off actor Ajith Kumar’s car race and seek fresh investments for Tamil Nadu. Keerthana, whose portfolio places her at the centre of the state’s investment-promotion efforts, was not part of the delegation.Reacting to Keerthana’s absence, Vaishnavi referred to TN minister Aadhav Arjuna’s statement that the industries minister had not travelled for “4 days due to health reasons” and questioned the reference to the four days.“Industrial minister has not come for 4 days due to health reasons, says Aadhav Arjuna! What is the explanation regarding those "4 days"? If it refers to a natural physiological change that occurs for women, like menstruation, then why should it be stated as the reason?” Vaishnavi said.She added, “Today's women athletes consider menstruation as a normal physiological process and plan their training and competitions accordingly. Doesn't even this basic understanding of women's physiology exist for a minister who oversees the sports sector?”Vaishnavi also questioned whether the actual reason for Keerthana’s absence had been clearly communicated, saying, “Especially, clearly informing the public about the real reason for a minister not attending an event is the transparent approach.”She further asked, “What is the real reason for industrial minister not coming? Will Aadhav Arjuna clarify?”Amid the controversy, TVK leader Kanimozhi Santhosh came out in support of Keerthana and said the minister had been recovering from a collarbone surgery when she missed the London visit.“As a woman, I want to say this because I witnessed it myself. I met myminister Keerthana at Kamatchi Hospital after her collarbone surgery. Doctors had advised around 20 days of rest, but within 4 days she was back at work because of her commitment to the state,” Santhosh said.She said Keerthana continued to coordinate Vijay’s London visit even while recovering in hospital.“Even while she was at hospital bed, she was coordinating the chief minister's London visit. Her first question every single day wasn't about her pain or her tablets; it was whether every company and every arrangement was on time. I told her to relax, she wouldn't,” Santhosh said.Taking aim at those who questioned the reason for Keerthana’s absence, Santhosh said, “And what struck me most is this: when minister Aadhav Sir said she was unwell for a few days, the opposition ecosystem didn't pause to ask about what was the reason, or recovery, or what she may have actually gone through. Their minds went straight to one reason: menstruation.”“That reflex, that a woman's absence can only ever mean one thing, says nothing about her and everything about your regressive mindset. Women are not defined by their cycles. We are leaders, professionals, mothers, daughters carrying illness, injury and duty all at once, and still showing up. Reducing a woman's every unexplained day to her biology is an old habit of attacking a woman's body when her work can't be faulted,” she added.Santhosh said Keerthana returned to work despite still recovering from the surgery.“4 days after, still recovering, on painkillers and still wearing a bandage, she went straight back to meeting companies and signing MoUs, one after another, without a pause,” she said.“This regressive mindset needs to stop. We should be celebrating women who continue to lead through difficult circumstances, not discussing their cycles. Women deserve better than this. Tamil Nadu deserves better than this,” Santhosh said.She concluded by apologising to Keerthana for making her medical condition public, saying, “Sorry Keerthana, I know you wanted to keep this private but I had to post this.”
Article Summary: DMK leader Vaishnavi questioned industries minister S Keerthana's absence from chief minister C Joseph Vijay’s recent London visit. The remarks have triggered a political controversy. TVK leader Kanimozhi Santhosh came out in support of the minister and said she had been recovering from a collarbone surgery when she missed the visit.

Article Title: A kidney wait since 2024 ends with an Army airlift and a rare double transplant
Article Text:
File photo: Organ donation (AI-generated)

NEW DELHI: An 18-year-old who had spent nearly two years waiting for a kidney, undergoing dialysis twice a week and with no family donor, received not one but two kidneys from a single brain-dead donor on Monday — after the organs were airlifted from Chandimandir to Delhi. Both kidneys were transplanted into Anil Yadav at Safdarjung Hospital, and he is doing well.The donor, 62-year-old Amar Chand, father of an Air Warrior, had undergone coronary artery bypass graft surgery last year and was on dual antiplatelet medication. He later slipped in his bathroom, suffered a head injury and brain haemorrhage, and was declared brain dead at Command Hospital (Western Command), Chandimandir. His organ donation helped save other lives. His liver was transported to Army Hospital (Research & Referral), Delhi, for transplantation, while both corneas were donated to Command Hospital, Chandimandir.His family’s decision to donate his organs set off a race against time. With Army support, the two kidneys were airlifted to Delhi and taken to Safdarjung Hospital, where doctors transplanted both into Anil, who has chronic renal failure.“This is the first en bloc renal transplant at the hospital, in which both kidneys from a donor with marginal renal function were implanted in a single recipient. With a severe shortage of organs nationwide, accepting marginal kidneys can help expand the donor pool and give more dialysis patients, many of whom wait for years, a chance at transplantation,” said Dr Himanshu, Professor & Academic Head, Department of Nephrology, VMMC & Safdarjung Hospital.“The patient is recovering well, with good renal function and urine output.”“The most difficult part of organ donation is counselling a grieving family to say yes within two hours,” said Col Anurag Garg, Transplant Coordinator and Palliative Physician at CHWC. “I have seen this in the Subedar’s family, a Colonel’s wife’s family and Air Warrior Ranbir’s case.”Anil had been waiting for a transplant since 2024, with no donor available in his family. Until Tuesday, twice-weekly haemodialysis had been part of his routine.For a teenager who had spent nearly two years waiting for a donor, the journey from a brain-dead donor in Chandimandir to a transplant table in Delhi took place in time to give him a chance at life beyond dialysis.
Article Summary: Anil Yadav had been waiting for a transplant since 2024, with no donor available in his family. Amar Chand, 62, had undergone coronary artery bypass graft surgery last year and was on dual antiplatelet medication. He later slipped in his bathroom, suffered a head injury and brain haemorrhage, and was declared brain dead. His family’s decision to donate his organs set off a race against time.

Article Title: PM Modi likely to visit Canada in December to lock in trade deal: Canadian PM Carney
Article Text:
PM Modi and Canadian PM Mark Carney (File photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is expected to visit Canada in December to seal the trade deal between New Delhi and Ottawa, Canadian PM Mark Carney said on Tuesday.Speaking on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, Carney said that the relationship between India and Canada is "exceptionally important" and claimed that both countries are looking to reach a trade deal by the end of the year."We're making good progress in our trade negotiations with India. It is an exceptionally important relationship, on many, many levels. People-to-people levels, security levels and also trade and economic," Carney said."He (PM Modi) will be visiting Canada around that time. I very much look forward to hosting him," he added.This comes after Union commerce minister Piyush Goyal said that India and Canada have agreed to fast-track negotiations for a comprehensive economic partnership, with the next round of talks scheduled to begin on October 5.Goyal said he had concluded the fourth round of negotiations for the proposed trade agreement with his Canadian counterpart, minister of international trade Maninder Sidhu, in Mumbai last week."I have concluded the fourth round of negotiations for the Canada trade deal with my counterpart Mr Maninder Sidhu in Mumbai on Friday. Very productive discussions and both sides have resolved to fast-track negotiations, in view of which our team is now slated to go for the fifth round," he said."Fifth of October. So you can see that as the progress is taking shape, the speed of negotiations with Canada is also improving. Let's see, the next 90 days should be a very defining period in the Canada-India relationship," the minister said.India and Canada have discussed a comprehensive trade pact for more than a decade. Negotiations were formally relaunched in March 2022, with the two sides also pursuing an Early Progress Trade Agreement as an interim step. Nine negotiating rounds were held between 2022 and 2023 before the process was paused in August 2023 amid a period of strain in bilateral relations.Trade talks between India and Canada restarted during the G20 summit in 2025 as both countries saw a thaw in diplomatic relations post the standoff with former Canadian PM Justin Trudeau who had blamed India for the killing of designated terrorist Hardeep Nijjar in Canada.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi is expected to visit Canada in December to seal the trade deal between New Delhi and Ottawa. Canadian PM Mark Carney said that the relationship between India and Canada is "exceptionally important" Carney claimed that both countries are looking to reach a trade deal by the end of the year.

Article Title: 'Look what happened in Bengal': Congress hits back after SP's 'only Akhilesh' pitch
Article Text:
Who will take on BJP in UP? SP-Congress spar over leadership role

NEW DELHI: The war of words between Congress and Samajwadi Party took a fresh turn over who will lead the fight against the Yogi Adityanath-led BJP in Uttar Pradesh assembly polls.The latest disagreement started after SP MP Iqra Hasan said Congress "can't achieve much on its own" and claimed that party chief Akhilesh Yadav was the only leader who could defeat the BJP in Uttar Pradesh. Congress leaders quickly pushed back.Congress MP Imran Masood said, "She (Iqra Hasan) also cannot do it alone. What is the problem with that? Iqra is our child. She is like our niece.""People from the Trinamool Congress were also saying a lot. Look at what happened in Bengal. Let us move together, and we will remain in peace," he added.Congress leader Udit Raj also questioned Iqra's claim, pointing to the SP's performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha election."That may be her (Iqra Hasan's) own statement, but we can understand this through an example: when the alliance was formed in 2024, the Samajwadi Party won 36 seats. What was its performance before that? The Samajwadi Party had only six MPs in 2019.So, in politics, one plus one does not always make two; one plus one can make eleven. Therefore, I think she should correct her understanding," Udit Raj told IANS.The BJP has also joined the exchange, questioning whether the opposition parties can stay united. Uttar Pradesh BJP vice-president Neeraj Singh said, "Congress will not be able to achieve anything on its own across the country. And even if it forms an alliance with the Samajwadi Party or any other party in Uttar Pradesh, the people of Uttar Pradesh have already formed an alliance in their hearts with the BJP government.Iqra had made the remarks on Monday, saying, "It is an absolutely foolish statement. I think that if there is anyone in Uttar Pradesh who can defeat the BJP, it is only Akhilesh Yadav. Congress will not be able to do anything on its own. If the alliance remains, it will be very good; if it does not, it is a loss for them (Congress), not for us."The exchange comes as both parties prepare for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly election. While the BJP is preparing keep its foot strong in the state to have third-term in country's largest state assembly.
Article Summary: SP MP Iqra Hasan said Congress "can't achieve much on its own" and claimed that party chief Akhilesh Yadav was the only leader who could defeat the BJP in Uttar Pradesh. Congress leaders quickly pushed back, pointing to the SP's performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. BJP has also joined the exchange, questioning whether the opposition parties can stay united.

Article Title: Pakistan must take credible action on crossborder terror before world believes it: MEA
Article Text:
India slams Pakistan over Permanent Court of Arbitration ruling

India seeks constructive ties with Bangladesh

275 Indians missing in Nepal

India reiterates dialogue, diplomacy on Ukraine

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Pakistan needs to take credible action against cross-border terrorism before the world can believe what it says, the ministry of external affairs said on Tuesday, while hitting out at Islamabad over its claims regarding a recent decision by the Permanent Court of Arbitration.MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal accused Pakistan of “misrepresenting facts” and spreading “falsehoods” as part of its propaganda.“Pakistan has a habit of misrepresenting facts and propagating falsehoods to serve its malicious propaganda,” Jaiswal said.“For starters, the so-called ruling is not a ruling by the Permanent Court of Arbitration, as sought to be projected by the Pakistan minister. It is a ruling by an illegally constituted court. We see this as just one more attempt by Pakistan at distorting the reality,” he added.Jaiswal was responding to a question about Pakistan circulating a letter to the president of the UN Security Council regarding recent rulings related to the Permanent Court of Arbitration.His comments also came days after Pakistan increased the reward for information leading to the arrest or conviction of Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) chief Masood Azhar.India had last week described Pakistan's PKR 70 lakh reward for information on Azhar as a “phoney” move and asked Islamabad to take concrete action against the JeM chief.The Pakistan-based Jaish-e-Mohammed has been linked to several major terror attacks in India, including the 2001 Parliament attack and the attacks in Pathankot and Pulwama.The group was founded by most-wanted terrorist Masood Azhar.New Delhi has repeatedly called on Pakistan to take credible action against crossborder terrorism, saying Islamabad's actions would be a key test of the credibility of its claims.On India-Bangladesh relations, Jaiswal said New Delhi wants positive and constructive ties with Dhaka.“India seeks positive, constructive and forward-looking ties with Bangladesh,” he said.On Indians missing in Nepal floods, Jaiswal said an Indian forensic team was working with Nepalese authorities to identify those still unaccounted for.“As I told you last time, we had given you a figure of 275 Indian nationals who were missing. Over and above that, several other people from the Indian diaspora and persons of Indian origin are also missing,” he said.“We have a forensic team in Nepal that is working in Kathmandu in several laboratories along with their Nepali colleagues,” Jaiswal said.He said the Indian team was working on 3,000 samples and had so far arrived at more than 1,200 DNA profiles.“The work is going on, and regarding the missing Indian nationals and missing persons, we await to hear from the Nepali authorities,” he said.On the Ukraine conflict, Jaiswal said external affairs minister S Jaishankar met Ukrainian foreign minister Andrii Sybiha on Monday and discussed recent developments.“Yes, the external affairs minister met with the Ukrainian foreign minister yesterday. During the meeting, he discussed the recent developments in the conflict,” Jaiswal said.Jaishankar reiterated India's position that dialogue and diplomacy are the way forward for a peaceful resolution.“The external affairs minister once again put forth India's point that dialogue and diplomacy are the way forward for a peaceful resolution,” Jaiswal said.“India, as you know, is in touch with both sides, Ukraine and Russia, and we have told them that if there is any way that India can contribute, India is ready to do so,” he added.
Article Summary: Pakistan needs to take credible action against cross-border terrorism, India says. India accuses Pakistan of spreading "falsehoods" as part of its propaganda. India wants positive and constructive ties with Bangladesh. India working with Nepalese authorities to identify those still unaccounted for.

Article Title: The Revisit: 125 shells, 10 minutes and a German attack on Madras - when WWI reached India
Article Text:
German cruiser SMS Emden that bombarded the city during the WWI on September 22.

The warship that did not look German

130 shells in one night

From harbour to high court

A city already preparing to flee

Why did Emden leave?

The word 'Emden' survives

The night war came home

When World War I broke out in Europe in July 1914, Madras was thousands of kilometres away from the battlefields. Yet there was little certainty among British authorities that the war would remain confined to Europe. The city's strategic importance as a major port made it vulnerable, and within weeks, residents were being advised to move towards safer places in the hinterland.By September, the anxiety had become real enough for some families to leave.Among them were the grandparents of PD Balaji, professor and head of the department of ancient history and archaeology at the University of Madras. Speaking to The Times of India in 2017 , Balaji recalled that his grandparents lived in Royapettah and moved to Salem briefly, taking some valuables with them because they feared Madras could come under attack.Their fears were realised on the night of September 22, 1914, when the German cruiser SMS Emden appeared off the Madras coast and opened fire.The attack lasted only a short time, but it became one of the most remarkable episodes of India's experience of World War I.The Emden had already been operating in the waters around the Indian subcontinent, attacking shipping before turning towards Madras. But the cruiser had an unusual advantage: it did not necessarily look like an enemy vessel from a distance.Historian Venkatesh Ramakrishnan told TOI that the Emden had a dummy fourth funnel, which made the German cruiser appear like a British ship.That deception was particularly useful in the busy waters of the region."Some enemy ships even saluted it during navigation," Ramakrishnan told TOI.The disguise allowed the cruiser to move through waters where a genuine German warship might otherwise have attracted immediate attention. By the time it approached Madras, the British authorities were facing a vessel that had managed to exploit both surprise and confusion.At around 9.30 pm, the attack began.The precise nature of the German target remains one of the interesting questions surrounding the bombardment. Some accounts have suggested that Fort St George was the intended target, while historian Venkatesh Ramakrishnan offered a different explanation.According to Ramakrishnan, Captain Karl von Müller did not necessarily direct his guns at one particular building."The Emden's captain Karl von Muller did not aim at any particular target. The shells were fired on any structure that was illuminated by the lighthouse," he told TOI.Around 130 shells were fired that night, according to Ramakrishnan.One struck a storage tank belonging to the Burmah Oil Company near the harbour. The tank caught fire, and the blaze continued for three days, turning the attack into a highly visible spectacle for the city.A separate 2014 TOI report, quoting historian V Dhivakar, put the number of shells at at least 125, fired within around 10 minutes. Dhivakar said the shells hit oil tanks containing approximately 350,000 gallons of oil.Whatever the precise count, the scale of the bombardment was remarkable for an attack that lasted only a short period.The German cruiser had sailed close enough to Madras to fire into the city and then withdrew before the British could mount an effective response.The attack was not confined to the waterfront.According to Ramakrishnan, shrapnel struck several parts of Madras, including the High Court, General Hospital, Vepery, Haddows Road, Poonamallee High Road, the gun battery at Royapuram, Casa Major Road and George Town.The geography of the damage is significant because it demonstrated how a naval attack on the harbour could quickly become a city-wide shock.For residents, the source of the explosions was initially not something they could easily understand. The war had until then existed largely in newspapers and official announcements. Suddenly, its sound could be heard across Madras.And the sight of the oil tank burning for days provided a lasting reminder that the British Empire's war had reached the Indian coast.The Emden attack did not come completely out of the blue.Anxiety had spread through Madras in the weeks following the outbreak of World War I. British authorities had advised residents to move to safer locations in the hinterland because of fears that enemy forces could attack the city.The exodus had already begun when the German cruiser struck.For families who had left, the decision suddenly appeared prescient. For those who remained, the bombardment reinforced fears that the Emden might return or that other German vessels could attack the city.The account of Balaji's grandparents provides a glimpse into what that uncertainty meant at an individual level. They left their Royapettah home for Salem and carried valuables with them, not knowing how long they would have to stay away.This was not merely a military episode. It had begun affecting ordinary civilian decisions.The attack also produced a question that historians continue to debate: Why did the Emden withdraw so quickly?The cruiser had managed to reach Madras, fire more than a hundred shells and hit important infrastructure. Yet it did not remain to inflict prolonged damage.Historian V Dhivakar challenged the later British explanation that Emden withdrew because of the British response.“After Emden reached a safe distance, the British started responding towards what for them was an unknown object in the dark far out at sea,” Dhivakar told TOI.He argued that the German cruiser could potentially have inflicted considerably more damage had it remained longer.The question becomes more intriguing when the Emden's capabilities are considered. Dhivakar described the cruiser as a formidable warship for its time, armed with ten 10.5cm guns and two torpedo tubes.Why Muller chose to stop when he did remains one of the enduring mysteries of the Madras raid.The Emden story also acquired an Indian revolutionary dimension through Chempakaraman Pillai, an Indian-born political activist and revolutionary who was living in Germany.A persistent claim has suggested that Pillai helped the Germans plan the Madras attack or was aboard the Emden.But the evidence cited by Dhivakar does not establish that.He told TOI that Pillai was not aboard the Emden during its wartime operations. Dhivakar referred to a book by Hellmuth von Mucke, the ship's vice-commander, which recorded several incidents aboard the cruiser without mentioning Pillai.Mucke did, however, refer to an Indian passenger who provided information.That detail has helped keep the Indian connection alive, but it does not prove that Pillai himself was involved in the attack.The most curious legacy of the raid may have been linguistic.The name Emden became part of popular usage in southern India, particularly in Tamil, where it came to be associated with someone formidable, daring or intimidating.The German cruiser therefore outlived its own military career in an unexpected way.The ship was eventually cornered and destroyed later in 1914, but its name had already acquired a place in Indian memory.For Madras, meanwhile, the physical reminders of the bombardment became part of the city's history. The High Court was among the places struck by shrapnel, while accounts of the attack have continued to document the damage caused across the harbour and surrounding neighbourhoods.The Emden attack did not change the outcome of World War I. It did not result in the capture of Madras, nor did it lead to a prolonged German campaign on the Indian coast.Its significance was different.It showed that a war that seemed distant and European could reach an Indian city with little warning. It exposed the vulnerability of a major colonial port, sent residents fleeing towards the interior and forced the British to confront the possibility that India's coastline could become part of the global conflict.For the people of Madras, September 22, 1914, was therefore not simply another date in the history of World War I.It was the night when the distant war suddenly became local: when a German cruiser appeared off the coast, 130 shells tore into the city, a Burmah Oil tank burned for three days, shrapnel reached the High Court and other parts of Madras, and a word that once belonged to a German warship entered the vocabulary of southern India.
Article Summary: German cruiser SMS Emden opened fire on Madras on September 22, 1914. Around 130 shells were fired on the city in a short period of time. Shrapnel struck the High Court, General Hospital, Vepery and Poonamallee High Road. One tank caught fire, and the blaze continued for three days.

Article Title: 'Bring your sisters too, our boys are ready': BJP MLA's garba remark on Muslim men sparks row
Article Text:
BJP MLA Rameshwar Sharma's garba comment sparks row

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A remark by Bharatiya Janata Party MLA Rameshwar Sharma on Muslim men attending Garba events sparked a political row on Monday. Speaking at a public event, the Bhopal MLA said Muslims were welcome to attend Garba and added that they should be “welcomed” permanently.Sharma then said: “Why do Muslim boys alone want to come to Garba? Bring your sisters and daughters along from home too, our boys are also ready.”Later, standing by his statement, Sharma said that if "Muslims have developed so much love and attachment to Sanatan, then kindly, why do only their boys come? Come, bring your sisters and daughters, bring your mothers and fathers. And don't come to watch Garba, but yourself perform the worship festival of the Goddess, play Garba, take Maa Jagdamba's prasad..."The remarks drew criticism from AIMIM state president Mohsin Ali Khan who said that Rameshwar Sharma's comments works "to divide the country"." I want to tell Rameshwar Sharma ji that what he has said definitely works to divide this country. He should now take this up with his senior leaders in the Bharatiya Janata Party. He should talk to Mukhtar Abbas Naqvi. He should talk to Shahnawaz Hussain, who has promoted interfaith harmony...Sothe question arises today: Article 25 gives every citizen of this country the freedom to wear what they want, to follow whatever religion they choose, and the freedom to marry people of any religion," he said.Condemning the statement, he said, "Inter-faith marriage is allowed. The Special Marriage Act provides the freedom to do so. Rameshwar Sharma ji needs to read the Constitution...Rameshwar Sharma ji only talks about attacking the Constitution, about appeasement, and about pitting two religions against each other.We condemn and oppose all those people who work to divide this country."All India Imam Association president Maulana Sajid Rashidi in turn asked Sharma if he was ready to send his daughters and sisters to a mosque. This BJP MLA Rameshwar Sharma, who said, 'Bring your sisters and daughters'... I want to ask him, can you send your sisters and daughters to a mosque? If you can, then send them. We will give them good education, teach them good values, explain to them how to live in this world, how to prepare for the hereafter, and how to face Allah. We will teach them about Islam, about faith, and how to live a good life...," he said.
Article Summary: Bhopal MLA Rameshwar Sharma said Muslims were welcome to attend Garba and added that they should be “welcomed” permanently. Sharma then said: “Why do Muslim boys alone want to come to Garba? Bring your sisters and daughters along from home too, our boys are also ready”

Article Title: Rajya Sabha polls: Dates announced for 12 seats in UP, Uttarakhand, Bengal
Article Text:
The Election Commission of India (ECI) has announced the biennial elections for 11 Rajya Sabha seats, along with a by-election for one seat from West Bengal, on October 16.

NEW DELHI: Election Commission on Tuesday announced elections to 12 Rajya Sabha seats across Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and West Bengal on October 16.The polls will cover 10 seats in Uttar Pradesh, one in Uttarakhand and a bypoll to one seat in West Bengal. The notification will be issued on September 29, nominations can be filed until October 6 and counting will take place on October 16, the poll panel said.In Uttar Pradesh, the members retiring include BJP leaders Arun Singh, Geeta Shakya, Neeraj Shekhar, Brijlal, BL Verma, Seema Dwivedi and Hardeep Singh Puri, Samajwadi Party leader Ram Gopal Yadav and BSP's Ramji Gautam.The seat held by former Uttar Pradesh deputy chief minister Dinesh Sharma has been vacant since September 11, when his resignation took effect following his appointment as lieutenant governor of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.In Uttarakhand, BJP member Naresh Bansal's term is also ending.Of the 10 outgoing Uttar Pradesh seats, eight are held by BJP, while the Samajwadi Party and BSP hold one each. Based on the current assembly arithmetic, BJP-led alliance is expected to win eight seats, while the Samajwadi Party could secure two.The outcome could leave BSP without representation in the Rajya Sabha as it does not have the numbers to retain Gautam's seat on its own.BSP currently has no MLA in Uttar Pradesh following the death of its lone legislator, Uma Shankar Singh, in August. The party also did not have the numbers to elect a Rajya Sabha member on its own in 2020. However, BJP had fielded only eight candidates for the 10 seats then, allowing BSP's Ramji Gautam to win.BJP is also comfortably placed to retain the Uttarakhand seat.The West Bengal bypoll was necessitated by the resignation of Rukmini Mallik, popularly known as actor Koel Mallick, on July 16. The winner will serve the remainder of the term until April 2, 2032.With a clear majority in the West Bengal Assembly, the ruling BJP is set to wrest the seat from the Trinamool Congress.
Article Summary: Election Commission announces elections to 12 Rajya Sabha seats on October 16. Polls will cover 10 seats in Uttar Pradesh, one in Uttarakhand and one in West Bengal. Members retiring include BJP leaders Arun Singh, Geeta Shakya, Neeraj Shekhar and BL Verma.

Article Title: A weathered Wyoming cabin used as a storage shed turned out to be a 140-year-old Chinese laundry; after an eight-year rescue effort, the building has been moved to a museum for restoration
Article Text:
The building has moved to Pioneer Village for restoration and display. (Pictures: Cowboy state daily)

How Sam Sing went from gold fields to laundry

Baths cost 25 cents in 1903

The Chinese laundry and bathhouse as it appeared when it was still being used as a storage shed.

Restoration work still remains

Preserving Sing’s story

A weathered cabin that spent decades being used as a storage shed behind a building on Main Street in Lander, Wyoming, has been identified as a late 19th-century Chinese laundry and bathhouse. The building belonged to Sam Sing, one of Lander’s early and influential residents.The small log cabin was donated to the Fremont County Pioneer Museum about eight years ago by property owner Tony McRae. The donation began a long effort to raise money, move the structure and preserve it. The building has now been moved to the museum’s Pioneer Village, where it will be restored and turned into an exhibit.Sing was among about 30 Chinese residents living in the town, which had a population of around 1,000 at the time. Historical records describe the Chinese residents as important contributors to the growing community, although they also faced restrictions, discrimination and hostility.Museum Director Randy Wise said Sing played a role in improving Lander. One example was his support for concrete sidewalks at a time when many Western towns relied on wooden boardwalks. According to Wise, “Sing said we, as a developing community, needed these.We needed to keep improving the community. So he was very interested in helping the community grow.”Sing was born Sing Yee Wind in Canton Province, China, in 1859. He later travelled to America, where he worked in California’s gold fields. He eventually went to South Pass City in Wyoming, joining others hoping to make money from the mining boom there.The boom did not last long, and Sing later moved to Lander. He worked as a cook at the Lander Hotel while continuing to look for gold and other valuable minerals. His training as a geologist also helped him recognise areas around Lander that had oil and gas deposits.Sing bought several valuable claims after recognising the potential of those deposits. However, he did not depend entirely on speculation. After saving enough money from his work at the hotel, he started a laundry and bathhouse in the small log cabin that has now been moved to the museum.The business provided services that were difficult and time-consuming for many households at the time. Laundry could require people to carry large amounts of water, cut wood, boil heavy pots and scrub clothes on metal washboards using lye.Bathing was also not as simple as it is today because many homes did not have running water. Sing could therefore earn money by providing baths, using tubs, soap, water and wood to heat it.Early advertisements show that Sing offered baths seven days a week for 25 cents each in 1903. The price later increased to 40 cents.His laundry and bathhouse originally stood on Main Street. It was later moved to the back of the McRae Pharmacy lot, where it remained for decades.That location may have helped save the building. It eventually became little more than a storage shed and attracted little attention. When McRae sold the main part of his business lot to Gannett Peak Sports, he still had items stored inside the old building and kept it where it was.“He was using the laundry as a storage shed, basically,” Wise said. “So nobody really paid much attention to it.”McRae eventually cleared the building and recognised its historical importance. About eight years ago, he approached the museum about taking it over. The museum agreed, but moving the old structure required money for both the relocation and a new concrete pad.The Lander Ambassadors raised just over $20,000 for that stage of the project. The historic cabin has now reached its new home at Pioneer Village.The building needs considerable work before it can become a museum exhibit. Some of the logs near the ground have rotted and will need to be replaced. The chinking between the logs also needs to be renewed, while the roof will be inspected to see whether repairs are required.Once the building is made weather-tight, the museum plans to replace bay doors that were added later. They will be replaced with a single door and a window on each side, which Wise said would be more historically accurate.The museum does not yet have photographs showing exactly what Sing’s laundry looked like when it was operating. If no original photographs are found, the restoration will have to be based on what an 1800s laundry in Lander would have looked like.The museum already has some original items from Sing’s laundry, along with other objects from the period. These include a working water pump. Wise said the building was close to Dickinson Creek, which runs through Lander, so Sing probably collected much of his water from the creek and may also have used a hand pump.The move has also given Pioneer Village a way to tell the story of Lander’s early Chinese residents. The village has around a dozen buildings preserving different parts of the town’s history, but this is the first building there connected to the Chinese community.Sing faced discrimination despite his standing in the community. Some children mocked him for his broken English and Chinese clothing, while he was robbed more than once. The windows of his laundry were also frequently broken by vandals.Despite those experiences, Sing remained in Lander and worked to improve the community. He never married and had no children. When he died on July 4, 1926, his brother travelled from Canton, buried him and returned to China. Sing’s headstone at Mount Hope Cemetery carries his Chinese name and an inscription in Chinese script.Wise expects the restoration of the laundry to take about a year and said more fundraising will be needed. The immediate focus is on protecting the structure from the weather.“There’s an argument to be made that moving a historic building kind of degrades its integrity,” Wise said. “I understand that argument. But the building probably would not have survived.”He added, “The building will be safe here for many, many decades so people can learn another little part of Lander history.” Once restored, the cabin will preserve not only the story of Sam Sing’s laundry and bathhouse, but also a lesser-known chapter of Lander’s Chinese community and its role in the town’s early development.
Article Summary: Building belonged to Sam Sing, one of Lander's early and influential residents. The small log cabin was donated to the Fremont County Pioneer Museum about eight years ago. The building has now been moved to the museum’s Pioneer Village, where it will be restored and turned into an exhibit.

Article Title: In 2012, NFL legend Joe Thomas bought a 1,200-acre Wisconsin farm with five cows and a bull; 14 years later, Hall of Fame Farms spans 4,100 acres and raises hundreds of cattle, including Wagyu
Article Text:
From football to farming

A different kind of Hall of Fame career

What happens on the farm

Building something beyond football

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former Cleveland Browns star Joe Thomas has taken an unexpected turn after retiring from football, trading the NFL field for life on a Wisconsin farm. The Pro Football Hall of Famer is the owner of Hall of Fame Farms, a cattle operation located in the state’s Driftless Region. Thomas spent 11 seasons with the Browns before retiring in 2018 and was inducted into the Hall of Fame in 2023. According to Fox News, his interest in farming grew while he was still playing, eventually leading him to build a substantial agricultural operation with his family. Farm Progress has also reported on Thomas’ work on the farm and his approach to raising cattle.Thomas, who grew up in Wisconsin, has spoken about wanting to own land long before his NFL career ended. He purchased the original property in 2012, while still playing for Cleveland, and initially started with just a handful of cattle.What began as a family farm eventually developed into a much larger agricultural operation. Fox News reported in September 2026 that the property has grown from the original 1,200 acres to roughly 4,100 acres and now includes hundreds of cattle, with Wagyu increasingly becoming a focus of the business.The transition also reflects a broader change in Thomas’ life after football. Following his retirement, he became increasingly interested in food, nutrition and the way cattle are raised. Farm Progress reported earlier this year that Thomas and his farm team emphasize nutrition and individual attention when caring for the herd.Thomas’ football résumé gives the farm its distinctive name. Selected third overall by the Cleveland Browns in the 2007 NFL Draft, he played his entire 11-season career in Cleveland. The numbers remain remarkable. Thomas made 10 consecutive Pro Bowls, earned six first-team All-Pro selections and played 10,363 consecutive offensive snaps. The Pro Football Hall of Fame lists him as a member of its Class of 2023.That reputation for consistency has now become part of the identity of his agricultural business. Hall of Fame Farms presents the operation as a long-term family project rather than simply a celebrity venture, with Thomas and his wife, Annie, raising their children around the farm.The cattle operation places a significant emphasis on producing both Wagyu and Certified Angus beef varieties. As reported by Hall of Fame Farms, the cattle are raised on pasture before entering a corn-finishing phase, while the farm also utilizes carefully selected genetics combined with a tailored nutrition programme that was developed in collaboration with a dedicated cattle nutritionist. In addition to this, the company proudly claims to work with Full Blood Wagyu genetics, ensuring high-quality meat production.The approach taken by the farm is fundamentally centred around low-stress handling techniques and a strong focus on comprehensive animal care to promote the well-being of the cattle. As highlighted by Farm Progress, Thomas’ dedicated team prioritizes nutritional needs and provides personalized care for each individual animal within their herd. Currently, the business offers a diverse array of beef products to consumers, which includes a selection of Wagyu steaks, Certified Angus beef, a variety of smoked meats, and beef tallow. Furthermore, the farm has established an online platform that enables customers to conveniently order specific cuts of meat directly from the brand.For Thomas, the world of farming signifies not merely a definitive closure to his athletic career but rather the beginning of a revitalizing second chapter. The meticulous precision and unwavering consistency that characterized his tenure in the NFL have seamlessly transitioned into the philosophy he employs in his cattle operations.Additionally, the backdrop is critical to the entire undertaking. Hall of Fame Farms is nestled within the picturesque rolling hills and lush pasturelands of Wisconsin’s Driftless Region, where Thomas has steadily transformed a property acquired during his football years into a thriving, family-operated agricultural enterprise.Though his storied football career concluded in 2018, the journey into farming has continued to flourish and develop. What commenced with just a modest herd of cattle has blossomed into a noteworthy farming operation in Wisconsin, providing the former Browns tackle with a fresh platform to cultivate the legacy he once strived to establish on the football field.
Article Summary: Former Cleveland Browns star Joe Thomas has taken an unexpected turn after retiring from football. The Pro Football Hall of Famer is the owner of Hall of Fame Farms, a cattle operation located in the state’s Driftless Region. Thomas spent 11 seasons with the Browns before retiring in 2018 and was inducted into the Hall of fame in 2023.

Article Title: Greatest Family Inspiration: How LeBron James’ daughter Zhuri gave Savannah James the reason to pursue her latest business venture
Article Text:
LeBron James’ daughter Zhuri inspired Savannah James to invest in women’s volleyball. Image via: IMAGO / ABACAPRESS

Savannah James credits daughter Zhuri for inspiring her women’s volleyball investment

Savannah James joins Issa Rae as investor in League One Volleyball team

Who is Savannah James?

All about LeBron and Savannah James’ daughter Zhuri Nova

Savannah James’ investment in women’s volleyball has a personal reason. Her daughter, Zhuri James inspired Savanna to invest in the team. Savannah recently became an investor in LOVB Los Angeles, a professional League One Volleyball team, joining an ownership group that includes Alexis Ohanian and Issa Rae . For Savannah, the move is about more than becoming part of a new sports venture. It connects directly to the sport her youngest child has embraced.Zhuri has already developed a connection with LOVB after attending the league’s championship event and delivering the ceremonial first serve. Now, with LOVB Los Angeles preparing for its first season in 2026-27, Savannah sees an opportunity to support both her daughter and the wider growth of women’s volleyball.Savannah James did not need to look far for a reason to invest in LOVB Los Angeles. Her daughter’s experience with volleyball gave the decision a personal meaning.In a statement, Savannah explained how watching Zhuri play has shaped her view of the sport.“I’ve seen firsthand through my daughter Zhuri how powerful volleyball can be for young girls, the confidence, discipline and sense of community it creates,” Savannah said.The perspective has become central to Savannah’s decision to join the ownership group.She sees the investment as a way to help create a pathway for girls who want to follow the same sport.“I’m excited to be part of LOVB Los Angeles and to help build something special that girls like Zhuri can aspire to be part of one day.”Savannah also spoke about the decision in an Instagram post, making clear that Zhuri’s involvement with volleyball was a major factor.“It was important to me to make my investment with LOVB Los Angeles because my daughter is a volleyball player,” she said. “She is coming up alongside amazing athletes who deserve the recognition that they are getting right now.”She continued, “So, any chance that I have to be able to support that or stand behind it and do things that matter in that way, I am 1000% involved.”Zhuri already has a connection with LOVB. In April, she delivered the first serve at the LOVB Volleyball Championship in Long Beach, California, and later interviewed professional volleyball player Skylar Fields.Her involvement also stands out because basketball has been such a major part of the James family. LeBron James , Bronny James and Bryce James have all been connected to basketball, but Zhuri has taken a different sporting path.LeBron acknowledged that earlier this year when discussing his daughter’s basketball ability.“She’s a volleyball player, don’t get my wife mad,” he said. “My wife is done with basketball, she’s done with it.”LeBron also admitted that Zhuri has still absorbed plenty from growing up around basketball.“[Zhuri’s] a volleyball player. But she’s been around the game for a while, so she does got good handles and she’s good form, too. But my wife ain’t playing that. Not another one. She says that’s it.”For Savannah, the investment gives her a direct way to support something that has already become important to her daughter.Savannah is joining an ownership group led by Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian through his investment firm, Seven Seven Six. The group also includes Issa Rae, adding another prominent name to the ownership side of LOVB Los Angeles.Savannah shared her excitement about working alongside the group in an Instagram post.“So excited to be alongside Issa Rae and Alexis Ohanian in this journey,” James expressed.The investment comes ahead of LOVB Los Angeles’ first season. The team is scheduled to begin play during the league’s 2026-27 season, with home games set for the Intuit Dome in Inglewood, California.The franchise is also preparing for its connection with fans before the season begins. A Fan Fest is scheduled for Sept. 26, giving players an opportunity to meet supporters before the new campaign.Savannah also highlighted what the team already has in place, pointing to its coaching staff and playing roster.“We have amazing coaches, Olympic-level athletes, a roster that can’t be beat, honestly. So, so excited for you guys to join us this season,” she continued.Savannah James, born Savannah Brinson on Aug. 27, 1986, in Akron, Ohio, is an entrepreneur, philanthropist and the wife of NBA superstar LeBron James.Savannah and LeBron met while they were in high school and have remained together since then. They married in 2013 and have three children: Bronny, Bryce and Zhuri.While her family is closely associated with LeBron’s basketball career, Savannah has developed her own interests and projects. She has been involved in charitable and community initiatives, with a particular focus on education and women’s empowerment.She played a key role in launching the LeBron James Family Foundation and founded Women of Our Future, a mentorship program supporting young women in Akron.Savannah has also worked in design and interior decorating while developing interests in fashion and wellness. Her investment in LOVB Los Angeles adds another sports-related business venture to that wider portfolio.Zhuri Nova James is the youngest child of LeBron and Savannah James. She was born on Oct. 22, 2014, after her parents had already welcomed sons Bronny and Bryce.LeBron has spoken warmly about his daughter and the role she plays in his life.“My daughter is the greatest thing in my life, along with my boys,” LeBron told Access Hollywood in 2021. “So, whenever she smiles, it don't matter what I'm doing, it makes me happy.”Zhuri has grown up in the spotlight and has appeared alongside her family at events and in campaigns. She attended the ESPY Awards, accompanied LeBron to the premiere of Space Jam: A New Legacy and appeared in a 2023 Beats by Dre campaign with her family.She has also explored fashion. In 2020, Zhuri helped launch the Janie and Jack x Harlem's Fashion Row collection and spoke about her excitement surrounding the project.“I’m most excited about the fashion and talking to the designers,” she told PEOPLE. Zhuri also revealed that she had “practiced with” her mother, Savannah.Away from fashion, she launched an Instagram account and YouTube channel. Her YouTube series, All Things Zhuri, included videos featuring her interests, with LeBron appearing in one episode.But volleyball has emerged as the clearest sporting connection for Savannah’s daughter. LeBron has shared videos of Zhuri playing, including one in 2023 in which he cheered her on.“Another One in the making! Uh-Oh 😱!!” LeBron captioned a carousel of videos. “Let’s Gooooooo Munchin!! @allthingszhuri got NEXT!! 🏐 VIBES!! #JamesGang👑 #ZTheWarriorPrincess👸🏾.”That path now has a direct connection to Savannah’s latest investment. As LOVB Los Angeles prepares for its first season, Zhuri’s passion for volleyball has helped give her mother a personal reason to become part of the league’s next chapter.
Article Summary: Savannah James joins Issa Rae as investor in League One Volleyball team LOVB Los Angeles. LeBron James’ daughter Zhuri inspired Savannah James to invest in women’s volleyball. Savannah is joining an ownership group led by Reddit co- founder Alexis Ohanian through his investment firm, Seven Seven Six.

Article Title: Lakshya Sen’s eight-point comeback powers India into Asian Games badminton semis
Article Text:
Lakshya Sen

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

When India needed him most, Lakshya Sen rediscovered his fighting spirit.Battling injuries and a prolonged slump in form, the Almora shuttler produced one of the most dramatic comebacks of his career, clawing back from 13-19 down in the deciding game against Japan’s Kodai Naraoka to win eight points in a row and seal a stunning victory in the men’s team quarterfinal.That win powered India into the semi-finals as the men swept the host nation 3-0 to assure a second consecutive team medal. The result followed the Indian women’s exit from the competition as they lost 1-3 to the hosts.India had gone into the tie with real concern over the recent form of its top-ranked singles player coming into the Games. Facing a formidable Japanese lineup, the team needed Lakshya to deliver, with the doubles pairing of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, and the young Ayush Shetty, expected to take care of their respective ties.Lakshya, however, had to dig deep before producing his moment of magic.Trailing 13-19 in the decider, he reeled off eight consecutive points to stun Naraoka 11-21, 21-5, 21-19.Satwik and Chirag made it 2-0 for India with a hard-fought win over former world champions Takuro Hoki and Yugo Kobayashi. Ayush then moved India to the brink of victory with a straight-games win over Koki Watanabe, 21-10, 21-19.But the story of the day belonged to Lakshya.He looked out of sorts in the opening game, moving poorly around the court and lacking his usual aggression. A pep talk from chief coach Pullela Gopichand appeared to change the complexion of the contest.Lakshya returned for the second game with renewed energy and immediately took control, racing to a 7-1 lead and never allowing Naraoka to recover as he wrapped up the game 21-5.The momentum shifted again in the decider. Naraoka steadily built an advantage and was sitting comfortably at 19-13, just two points from victory. With India’s hopes resting on him, Lakshya produced the best stretch of the match.At 14-19, he took the risk of playing a cross-court smash to Naraoka’s forehand and followed it with another winner into the backhand corner. The Japanese shuttler then hit into the net before misjudging a line call, allowing Lakshya to draw level at 19-19.At 19-all, Lakshya produced another moment of brilliance, diving full length to retrieve a drop shot and push the shuttle towards the backline to earn match point at 20-19. Naraoka then erred at the net.“It was a memorable victory. Great to see the singles players and Satwik-Chirag win another medal for India. With two Asian Games medals, two Thomas Cup medals and two Badminton Asia medals, it has been a dream period for us. I am confident our team will go the distance,” chief coach Pullela Gopichand told TOI.India will face China in the semi-finals after the latter defeated South Korea 3-2. Indonesia will take on Thailand.The Indian women’s team saw its campaign end against Japan.World Championships bronze medallists Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand secured India’s lone point with a 21-17, 21-16 win over Yuki Fukushima and Mayu Matsumoto. PV Sindhu lost the opening singles to Akane Yamaguchi 23-21, 18-21, 11-21, while Unnati Hooda went down to Tomoka Miyazaki 16-21, 18-21, leaving Japan 2-0 ahead.Tanvi Sharma then lost the crucial fourth tie to Nozomi Okuhara 12-21, 10-21.The women’s semi-finals will see South Korea face Japan and China play Indonesia.
Article Summary: Lakshya Sen produced one of the most dramatic comebacks of his career. He fought back from 13-19 down in the deciding game against Japan’s Kodai Naraoka to win eight points in a row. That win powered India into the semi-finals as the men swept the host nation 3-0 to assure a second consecutive team medal.

Article Title: Harmanpreet’s India make history with record 147-run win, clinch Asian Games gold
Article Text:
Asian Games: Women's cricket delivers first gold medal

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Trust the women to lead the way. Proud to be part of the Indian contingent at the Asian Games, but with no athletes’ village and handed a tight schedule, the women’s cricket team had little opportunity to mingle with, interact with or watch the country’s other athletes.But on a sun-kissed Tuesday at the Korogi Sports Park here, Harmanpreet Kaur and her team gave the nearly 500-strong contingent a big reason to celebrate, winning India’s first gold of the Games with a dominant 147-run win, the highest margin of victory by runs in women’s T20 Internationals, over Sri Lanka in the final.The skipper was delighted that her team had struck India’s first gold.“It’s a big thing for me because our aim was to take back the gold. More importantly, we wanted to see our flag fly high. We didn’t think we would win the first gold. I’m sure our athletes will win many more gold medals,” Harmanpreet said.Unlike the other events they play in, there is no trophy to be lifted here. But Harmanpreet was more than happy to trade it for a gold medal.“When we win trophies, they go to the BCCI office,” she said with a laugh. “The biggest thing for us is to be part of the Games and take back a medal to frame and keep at home,” Harmanpreet said.The gold was not just a successful defence of a medal. It was a reminder, on an evening when their fellow athletes were scattered across the city and beyond, that the contingent could come together in celebration.“Looking at the overall calendar and our list of achievements, as cricketers, we always wanted to be part of the Asian Games, Commonwealth Games and the Olympics. We have always played bilateral series, the ICC World Cup and Asia Cup, but until the previous Asian Games, we didn’t know what it felt like to work hard for a medal. We feel lucky that we are getting these opportunities now. So we just want to take the positives from this. ”In a rematch of the previous edition of the Asian Games, India put up a commanding 216/3 before skittling out Sri Lanka for 69 in 15.4 overs on a ‘hybrid’ pitch that aided spinners. Smriti Mandhana led the charge with a 45-ball 79, hitting five fours and seven sixes, while Shafali Verma made 48 off 29 balls (3x4; 3x6).Richa Ghosh then provided the late fireworks, smashing an unbeaten 49 off just 22 balls.In reply, Sri Lanka struggled to cope with the turning track. Deepti Sharma led India’s spin quartet with 3/6, while Shafali (2/3), Shreyanka Patil (2/9) and Shree Charani (2/13) claimed two wickets apiece.On a surface that initially offered plenty to the batters, Shafali and Smriti needed little time to settle. Smriti opened her account with consecutive boundaries through point off Sugandika Kumari, and after Mithali Ayodhya kept Shafali quiet for an over, Smriti took the attack back to Sugandika with back-to-back sixes.The two then cleared the ropes with regularity before Chamudi Praboda broke the partnership, Shafali’s reverse sweep finding Kawya Kavindi at backward point.But the damage had been done. Smriti appeared set for a century before miscuing a slog sweep off Sugandika Kumari. Richa took over, adding the finishing flourish that lifted India past 200.Sri Lanka never got going in the chase. Apart from skipper Chamari Athapaththu, who made 29, and Kaushini Nuthyangana (14), none of their batters managed to reach double figures.As soon as Shreyanka rattled Kaushini Nuthyangana’s stumps to seal the gold, the tricolour began fluttering in the team dugout. Moments later, the players held it aloft in celebration.BRIEF SCORES: India 216/3 (Mandhana 79, Ghosh 49*, Shafali 48, Praboda 1-34) beat Sri Lanka 69 (Athapaththu 29, Deepti 3-6, Shafali 2-3, Patil 2-9, Charani 2-13) by 147 runs.
Article Summary: India beat Sri Lanka by 147 runs in women's T20 Internationals final. Smriti Mandhana top scored for India with 79 off 45 balls. Shafali Verma made 48 off 29 balls (3x4; 3x6) Richa Ghosh hit unbeaten 49 off just 22 balls for India.

Article Title: Elavenil Valarivan, Parth Mane miss podium after late charge falls short in 10m air rifle mixed event
Article Text:
The team of Elavenil Valarivan and Parth Mane finished fourth in the final of 10m air rifle mixed event at Asian Games 2026

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nagoya: The smiles on Elavenil Valarivan and Parth Mane’s faces as they left the qualification arena for the 10m air rifle mixed event made way for agony after the first five shots of the final at the Aichi Prefectural Shooting Range.On Tuesday, from bettering the Games record and finishing second in the qualifiers to ending fourth, well short of the podium, the result came down to consistency, or the lack of it.The shooters, who won silver medals over the past two days, were on point in the qualifiers with 634.6, behind China (638.9). Both teams bettered the Games qualification record, which stood at 634.4.In the final, Japan took the last spot after Vietnam were disqualified because their competition suits failed to meet international standards.After the first five shots, India were last with 103.6, 0.3 behind the hosts. They played catch-up, by which time Korea, who finished third, had taken a two-point lead.Elavenil and Mane made a late charge but failed to bridge the gap, finishing with 376.3. China took the gold with a world record of 507.1, while Korea and Japan settled for silver and bronze.The rifle team’s coach, Pooja Ghatkar, pinned the performance on inconsistency.“Elavenil did well in the qualification. But both shooters were not able to settle into their positions in the final and their shots were all over the place,” she said.She also felt the timeout strategy misfired.

NEW DELHI: India's star weightlifter Mirabai Chanu won her maiden Asian Games medal on Wednesday, claiming silver medal in the women's 49kg category at the Nagoya City Trade and Industry Center in Aichi and Nagoya.Mirabai lifted a total of 198 kg in the event. Article Title: A 97-year-old Brisbane bowls club facing demolition is saved in a $6 million deal after Bowls Queensland rejected an offer $1 million higher to keep both greens
Article Text:
Griffin Hospitality plans to renovate the clubhouse, bar and kitchen while retaining the atmosphere and character associated with the club. The aim is to make the venue more welcoming for bowlers, families and visitors while keeping the sport at its centre.

A campaign that kept the greens alive

Plans for a renewed clubhouse

The committee stays on

For a club that spent years staring down the prospect of demolition, the future of Coorparoo Bowls Club now looks very different. The 97-year-old Brisbane institution will remain a place for bowls and community gatherings after the site was sold for $6 million to a local investor, ending plans that could have replaced the club with high-rise apartments, states the latest news report by ABC News. The deal preserves both bowling greens and gives the historic club a chance to enter its next chapter without losing the character that has defined it for generations.As per the ABC News report, the sale follows a multi-year campaign by the Coorparoo Bowls Club committee, which had been fighting to protect the venue and was facing eviction in May this year. Rather than see the site disappear under a redevelopment, the club will now remain in place under new ownership. Bowls Queensland reached the $6 million agreement with Coorparoo local Will Griffin of Griffin Hospitality Group after considering competing offers. The organisation rejected an offer that was $1 million higher, prioritising an agreement that would keep bowls operating at the site.That decision means both existing greens will stay. One will be available for competitions, while the other will cater to casual players, preserving the club's role for both organised games and everyday community use.The new ownership is expected to bring changes to the venue, but not a complete transformation, adds the online report. Griffin Hospitality plans to renovate the clubhouse, bar and kitchen while retaining the atmosphere and character associated with the club. The aim is to make the venue more welcoming for bowlers, families and visitors while keeping the sport at its centre. The plans also position the club as more than a sporting venue, with space for meals, social gatherings and community activities alongside regular bowls. For a property that had been facing a very different future, the approach offers a way to modernise the venue without erasing its history.The report also states that the committee that led the campaign to save Coorparoo Bowls Club will remain involved, signing a five-year lease to continue running the club. That arrangement keeps the people who have helped steer the club through its uncertain years connected to its future. With both greens protected, renovations planned and the existing committee remaining at the helm, Coorparoo Bowls Club has avoided demolition and secured a path forward. After nearly a century at the heart of the local community, the club will continue rolling bowls rather than making way for towers.Image Courtesy: ABC News
Article Summary: Coorparoo Bowls Club has been sold for $6 million to a local investor. The deal preserves both bowling greens and gives the historic club a chance to enter its next chapter without losing the character that has defined it for generations. The committee that led the campaign to save the venue will remain involved, signing a five-year lease to continue running the club.

Article Title: ‘We want to see him under pressure’: New Zealand coach lays down challenge for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
Article Text:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New Zealand head coach Rob Walter is keen to see how India’s teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi handles the challenge of pace and bounce when the two sides meet in the upcoming T20I series.Sooryavanshi has already made a name for himself with explosive performances in the IPL in 2025 and 2026, as well as at this year’s U19 World Cup. Those displays earned him his T20I debut against England in July.The teenager was part of India’s squad for the 3-0 T20I series win over Afghanistan and the narrow two-run victory over Japan in Sano, but did not feature in the playing eleven.Walter said he would be particularly interested in watching Sooryavanshi bat on the seam-friendly, bouncy New Zealand surfaces and also see how he responds if put under pressure.“Yes, I'd love to see him on some pace in bouncy wickets and see how different that looks. But he's an exciting player. You've seen him dominate against the world's best bowlers in the IPL. I think the challenge is always to see how that translates to different conditions and also how do we bowl to him in our conditions.“Again, secretly as a coach, you always want to see your players under a little bit of pressure and how we respond to that.So looking forward to it, if that is the case. If he's not here, they do have a lot of very good players other than him,” Walter told reporters on Wednesday.The New Zealand coach was also asked about the controversial wide call during India’s recent one-off T20I against Japan, which sparked considerable debate.Walter made it clear that he had not followed the match closely and had little interest in getting drawn into the controversy.“A very short segment (I watched). I saw there was some controversy around the wide ruling. But no, I didn't watch a hell of a lot of it, to be fair. The lesser the better, I think.”The upcoming series will also bring New Zealand back together for their first T20I engagement as a collective since the T20 World Cup final in Ahmedabad, where they suffered a heavy defeat to India.Walter acknowledged that losing a final naturally leaves a mark, but insisted the Black Caps' motivation for the home series is not centred on revenge.“I suppose it is there. No one likes to lose a final. I've done it twice, so I know all about it. But I think what comes first is representing the Black Caps and New Zealand well. So you've got a group of players who are always trying to do that first. Of course, if you manage to get a couple of victories at home, that would be great.“But taking care of the little steps in between now and then is the most important part. Being excited about representing again - it's been a while for some of the guys. Obviously it's the first time as a collective since the World Cup, with the majority of the squad that was in the World Cup to run out together.“So there's always something in it. It's not our major focal point, certainly not the things we speak about the most. Most importantly, we want to play good cricket and represent well,” he explained.
Article Summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi made his T20I debut against England in July. The teenager has already made a name for himself with explosive performances in the IPL in 2025 and 2026, as well as at this year’s U19 World Cup. New Zealand head coach Rob Walter is keen to see how the teenager handles pace and bounce.
