Article Title: 7 months on, Janakpuri road still a trap
Article Text:
The biker died on Feb 6. On Feb 9, Delhi Traffic Police issued an advisory saying excavation work on the stretch being carried out by DJB would require temporary traffic diversions and partial road closures for a week

TOI





NEW DELHI: The barricades are still there. So are the potholes, scattered signs of unfinished work, and air thick with dust.Seven months after a 25-year-old biker fell into an open construction pit and died on Prof Joginder Singh Marg in Janakpuri, the state of the road seems to have changed little. With its one side still blocked, the other is being used by traffic going to and fro, resulting in chronic snarls and chaos.From a distance, the barricades give the impression that the stretch where danger used to lurk has been cordoned off and work is progressing behind them. Walk closer, and the actual picture is different.Two uprooted trees lie behind the barricades, their trunks and branches left where they presumably fell. The pit dug up by Delhi Jal Board (DJB) in which the biker had fallen has been filled, but the road, whose surface has still not been evened out, remains out of bounds. At one corner behind the barricades, broken toilet seats, wooden planks and other discarded material have been left behind, giving the site the appearance of an informal dumping ground.The problems spill out beyond the barricades. As a result of the unfinished work, a portion on one side of the road is still out of bounds to commuters, reducing available space for traffic.On the open stretch, potholes, loose soil and dust make the daily commute an ordeal.Pedestrians, too, have little respite, with the ongoing work taking away valuable walking space. Rinku, who works as domestic help in nearby houses, said, “It feels like it will never get back to normal. We don’t even have a proper footpath.”Paramjeet Singh Sahni, a Janakpuri resident, said, “We use this road every day and end up suffering. Even seven months after the death of the biker, it has not been properly restored. It is full of congestion and dust. It may no longer have an open pit for someone to fall into, but the surrounding stretch still betrays unfinished work and poor upkeep.”Shopkeepers are also watching the condition of the road with concern, particularly with the festive season approaching and traffic expected to increase. Harpreet, who runs a shop nearby, said everyone wants a clean, usable road, able to handle an increased volume of traffic.The delay in the completion of ongoing work becomes starker when measured against what was originally announced. The biker died on Feb 6. On Feb 9, Delhi Traffic Police issued an advisory saying excavation work on the stretch being carried out by DJB would require temporary traffic diversions and partial road closures for a week.That one week has stretched into seven months. Traffic sources said advisories are tentative, while work was further delayed after a contractor’s tender was allegedly cancelled.So, for those using Joginder Singh Marg every day, the barricades have become part of their daily routine and are a reminder of the accident that exposed the stretch’s glaring safety lapses.Neither DJB nor PWD responded to’s queries on why the road remains unrestored or on the current progress of the work.
Article Summary: A 25-year-old biker fell into an open construction pit and died on Prof Joginder Singh Marg in Janakpuri. On Feb 9, Delhi Traffic Police issued an advisory saying excavation work on the stretch being carried out by DJB would require temporary traffic diversions. That one week has stretched into seven months.

Article Title: Beef must be kept in cold storage, only brief hanging ok: FDA
Article Text:
Beef cannot be kept outside the entire day as by the end of the day, it will degrade, said FDA

FDA: Label paneer as either dairy or analogue clearly





PANAJI: Beef sold at shops must be maintained in the cold chain, FDA director Shweta Desai said on Wednesday, responding to a question about beef being hung in shops for sale. “It’s ok to hang it for a little while (half an hour to one hour), but over a period of time it will get spoiled. It cannot be kept outside the entire day as at the end of the day, the quality will degrade,” she said.Desai said beef should be kept in a deep freezer or sold quickly to prevent spoilage.She added that meat and meat products should not be exposed to air and must be stored under controlled temperatures.Desai was speaking after a meeting with food business operators involved in the manufacture and supply of paneer and mawa in Goa, including sweet mart shops and various associations. The meeting was held to explain the advisory recently issued on analogue paneer and mawa.More than 50 operators and various associations attended.The FDA instructed operators to label paneer and mawa clearly as either ‘analogue’ or ‘dairy’ so consumers know what they are buying. FDA said this classification must also be stated on every consignment and reflected on bills.It added that, whether analogue or dairy, these products must be stored and maintained under the cold chain.For sweet shops, Desai said each tray must carry labels specifying whether items such as pedas and burfis are dairy-based or analogue, so customers can make informed purchases.“We have given them four days to comply, and from next week onwards, FDA officers will begin checking for compliance. Non-compliance will invite strict action as per the law.”
Article Summary: Beef sold at shops must be maintained in the cold chain, FDA director Shweta Desai said. Desai was speaking after a meeting with food business operators involved in the manufacture and supply of paneer and mawa in Goa. More than 50 operators and various associations attended the meeting.

Article Title: Xbox lays off 268 more employees across Halo Studios and other first-party studios; company says: This brings us roughly three-quarters of...
Article Text:
Xbox is now three-quarters of the way through its 3,200-job restructuring

Activision will build the next Halo game with a new team

Xbox is merging Forza studios and moving Obsidian under Bethesda

Ninja Theory faces closure after two failed sale deals

Microsoft is cutting another 268 jobs at Xbox, and the latest round lands hardest on the studio behind its most famous franchise. Halo Studios, formerly 343 Industries, is losing staff alongside other first-party teams and the Xbox Game Studios management and central functions layer. In the same move, the next mainline Halo game is being handed to Activision, the Call of Duty publisher.Xbox chief content officer Matt Booty announced the cuts in a memo to employees. They count towards the 3,200 role reductions that Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announced in July for Microsoft's 2027 financial year, which ends in June 2027. About 1,600 of those jobs went in the first round. "The actions completed since July, inclusive of the studio divestitures, bring us roughly three-quarters of the way through previously announced restructuring," Booty wrote.Activision is setting up a purpose-built Halo team, kept separate from its Call of Duty development. A small group at Halo Studios will stay on to support the community and the games already in players' hands. The shift comes just months after Halo: Campaign Evolved launched.Activision is also taking charge of World's Edge, the Age of Empires studio, and Rare, the developer of Sea of Thieves. Activision president Rob Kostich said the aim is to "make the greatest Halo game ever."Booty says the goal is to run fewer business units and bring together groups that already work closely. Bethesda now oversees Obsidian, which continues work on Grounded and a new Fallout project made with Bethesda Game Studios. King, the Candy Crush maker, absorbs Microsoft Casual Games, home to Solitaire and Minesweeper.Playground Games and Turn 10 Studios, partners on Forza for over a decade, will now operate as one studio handling both Forza and Fable.The plan to offload studios has had mixed results. Compulsion Games and Double Fine went independent in August with their IP, back catalogues and runway funding. Undead Labs has now followed on similar terms and, with a new publisher, will still release State of Decay 3 on Game Pass on day one.Ninja Theory, the Hellblade developer, was not as lucky. Two separate agreements to sell the studio fell through, so Xbox will begin consultation with employees on a proposed closure while exploring other paths. Talks over Arkane's future in France are expected to run until the end of the year.The reason behind all of this was laid out in Sharma's July memo. Xbox was operating at margins three to 10 times lower than comparable platform and publishing businesses, and in a typical year lost 64 cents for every dollar it invested in studios. Employees will gather at an October 6 town hall, where Booty plans to look ahead to what he calls one of the strongest game lineups in Xbox history. With a quarter of the cuts still to come, that lineup now carries the weight of the reset.
Article Summary: Halo Studios, formerly 343 Industries, is losing staff. Activision is setting up a purpose-built Halo team, kept separate from its Call of Duty development. Activision president Rob Kostich said the aim is to "make the greatest Halo game ever"

Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge
Article Text:
El Rubius reacted honestly after his elimination from MrBeast’s $1 million challenge, calling it “unfair” and claiming he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings. His response felt real and balanced, especially after MrBeast’s team later sent him a cake, softening the moment.

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit

El Rubius did not just walk away from MrBeast’s $1 million streamer challenge. He opened up. Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. It was not polished or carefully framed. It felt real, and that is exactly why it caught attention so quickly.The clip and his response have since fueled conversations across the streaming space. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. It went to the mods, the subs, and the non-subs alike."He further added, "I’m happy, of course, though admittedly, it was incredibly tough.I wasn't really a fan of the challenge itself, either. But then again... it was basically a three-against-one situation the entire time. I mean, they were targeting me specifically the whole way through. I kept trying to go after RaKai, but, well, he actually just got eliminated in the end. So, at least justice was served for Abraham. Abraham, if you’re watching this, we were all rooting for you, and standing right there with you."His message carried mixed emotions. There was disappointment, yes, but also pride in how he handled things. Giving away his $50,000 winnings to his community stood out as a gesture that meant more than the result itself.He continued with another honest note, saying, "And in the end, karma finally caught up with that little punk. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. Seriously, thank you for all the support and for just being there."He added, "Every time I asked for something in the chat or whatever it was, you guys were right there. You’re incredible. I’m a little disappointed in myself, personally, mostly for not performing better, but hey, I gave it my all, and we still walked away with $50,000, so we’ve got to look on the bright side. All right, guys, big hugs to all my brothers out there!"Interestingly, the story did not end with frustration. Later that day, Rubius revealed that MrBeast’s team had sent him a cake after his exit. It was a small gesture, but it shifted the mood. It showed that even in a high-pressure challenge, there is still room for respect.In the end, Rubius’ reaction felt honest and grounded. That is what stayed with people.
Article Summary: El Rubius was eliminated from MrBeast's $1 million streamer challenge. He called it "unfair" and said he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings.

But for a 25-year-old techie the craze for IPL tickets for RCB vs CSK turned too costly and he was duped for a massive Rs. 1.46 lakh.The techie, a resident of B Narayanapura, fell into a trap by a post posted by a fraudster who posed himself as a ticket seller on Instagram.As per a report in Deccan Herald, the techie alleged in a complaint to Mahadevapura Police that an individual claiming to be Sumit Biswal promised he could arrange IPL tickets along with food coupons.As per the techie, Biswal was introduced him as a senior supervisor for ticket counter at M Chinnaswamy Stadium"He asked me to come near the stadium gate number 10, saying someone would deliver the tickets within minutes, and even sent an email confirmation to gain my trust," the complainant told Deccan Herald."Initially, I agreed to buy two tickets for Rs 3,700 each,but he kept asking for more money under various pretexts such as refundable security deposits, additional ID cards and food coupons.Trusting him, I made multiple payments - even using my mother’s bank account after exhausting my own limits—and ended up transferring around Rs 1.46 lakh," he added.Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s incisive spell of 3-41, coming after a marauding batting show from Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal, propelled Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) to a commanding 43-run victory over Chennai Super Kings (CSK) in their IPL 2026 encounter at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium on Sunday.The contest saw RCB’s batting unit dismantle CSK’s attack with relentless hitting, as David’s 70 not out off just 25 balls and Patidar’s unbeaten 48 off only 19 balls provided for the late fireworks after Padikkal’s fluent 50 off 29 balls had set the tone for the daunting total.Their combined effort lifted RCB to a daunting 250/3, thus setting a new record for highest total in IPL 2026. Article Title: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture
Article Text:
A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Instead of conflict, the exchange highlights shared influence and mutual awareness. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration rather than ownership.

Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends

The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. It is a mere, everyday talk that seems almost novel nowadays, in the age of internet, which is overflowing with content. The scene is easy-going, the tone of the narrative is straightforward, and the characters appear more concerned with conversation than combat.The message that is being addressed is the flow of the conversation. It discusses internet culture, the way people communicate with one another and the place of trends. Rather than bringing out a debate, the encounter towards curiosity. It quietly brings attention to something that a lot of people who use the internet notice but don't often say out loud. People in different communities often have a bigger impact on each other than they think.The conversation begins with a confident and lighthearted comment from one of the trans women present. She says, "You know that trans women are like the OG lip masters, right? We are very talented in the program. Like, I do the peptides, I'm on Zeta." Her tone carries a mix of pride and humor, setting a relaxed vibe at the table.Clavicular responds in a way that keeps the mood steady but adds a different angle.He says, "That is funny because you guys were using a lot of the words in like the South Korean subreddits in like 2014." It’s not confrontational. If anything, it feels like an observation. He points to how certain words and ideas may have traveled across different online spaces over time.Another voice joins in and brings the moment full circle. "Guys, we're like the OGs. I saw a couple of posts about that. We're like copying each other." That line hits in a simple but honest way. It reflects something familiar. Online culture is rarely created in isolation. It grows through sharing, borrowing, and sometimes even unknowingly repeating.That's what makes the clip so powerful. It doesn't want to make a point or win an argument. It only shows a group of people talking, listening, and figuring something out together.This moment feels different in a space where viral content often leads to fights. It reminds people that conversations can be calm, thoughtful, and still important. And sometimes, that honest silence is what makes it work.
Article Summary: A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration.

Article Title: ‘Firearms, knife and more’: How 3 men posing as cops turned 17-year-old’s birthday outing into a nightmare
Article Text:
Image Used For Representational Purpose Only

One of accused arrested after exchange of fire

Increased CCTV coverage More security personnel present Better lighting Regular police patrols 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





NEW DELHI: Out to celebrate her birthday with a friend after visiting Kalkaji Temple, a 17-year-old girl from Faridabad was allegedly raped by three men posing as cops in Aastha Kunj Park near the bustling Nehru Place Monday evening. Police arrested one accused after an exchange of fire Tuesday morning and two others soon after.The girl, a student of Class XI, had gone to the park with a male friend, also 17, after visiting the temple around 7pm. They entered the park from a gate that’s close to Lotus Temple. Their nightmare began unfolding when the three men in plainclothes allegedly approached them and began intimidating them. They told them they were minors and doing something “wrong” and that their parents would be informed. They said a case would be registered and threatened to call the PCR, police said.They then allegedly manhandled and slapped the girl’s friend before taking her away to a secluded part of the park. Police said one of the men, Asif, threatened her with a firearm and a knife and raped her. The other two, Hemant and Mukesh, then allegedly took turns to rape her. The three men then fled after threatening the girl and her friend.The incident happened between 7.30pm and 8pm.The girl called the PCR around 8.45pm and a team from Amar Colony police station, about 2km away, rushed to the spot. Police recorded the girl’s statement.Joint commissioner of police (southern range) Vijay Kumar said she was examined at AIIMS and crime and FSL teams inspected the scene. Some used condoms were found on the spot.A case was registered under BNS sections 70(2) for gang rape; 61(2) for criminal conspiracy; 115(2) for voluntarily causing hurt; and 351(3) for criminal intimidation along with sections 6 and 17 of Pocso Act.Police formed teams to trace the accused. Clues provided by the girl about the clothes the men were wearing and the names with which they were addressing each other proved critical in helping police make headway. With the help of some local enquiries and CCTV footage from the vicinity, where Hemant and Mukesh, who are brothers, were spotted, police were soon on the trail of the criminals.A breakthrough came around 6am Tuesday when a team received information about Asif having been spotted near DM Office Road in Amar Colony and laid a trap, said an officer.When police finally intercepted Asif and asked him to surrender, they said he fired three rounds. One bullet hit head constable Rajesh, who was wearing a bulletproof jacket. Rajesh then fired two rounds, one of which hit Asif in his right leg, police said.He was taken to AIIMS Trauma Centre for treatment. As Asif began singing, police tracked down Hemant and Mukesh and arrested them later in the day.Police said Asif is a wholesaler of vegetables at Okhla mandi. He is married and has a daughter. Hemant’s father, advocate J R Dhankar, has told police that his son is a lawyer, a claim that police are verifying. Mukesh is a BSc student.Dhankar has accused police of framing his sons. “One of my sons is an advocate practising at Saket courts while the other is pursuing BSc in mathematics. Police picked them up from their home in Sriniwaspuri early in the morning without informing us. Their statements were taken forcibly. This is a conspiracy. They did not know Asif. They were at home Monday and did not go out,” he alleged.Police, however, claim that the three men have said during interrogation that they had met each other about three months ago.Aastha Kunj, unlike its name which spells hope, has gained notoriety over the years for lack of security. Over the past few years, several cases of robberies, snatchings and harassment have been reported here.The park, which was meant to serve as a link to Kalkaji Temple, Baha’i Temple (Lotus Temple) and Iskcon Temple, and also gives access to Nehru Place District Centre and the extended food and entertainment zones, is managed by DDA.It is spread across 140 acres and has 29 entry points. Police said they have been regularly asking DDA to strengthen security measures, including improving CCTV coverage and lighting.When asked about this, DDA told TOI that it was undertaking a “comprehensive assessment of security manpower and deployment requirements”.
Article Summary: A 17-year-old girl from Faridabad was allegedly raped by three men posing as cops in Aastha Kunj Park near the bustling Nehru Place Monday evening. One of the men, Asif, threatened her with a firearm and a knife and raped her. The other two, Hemant and Mukesh, then allegedly took turns to rape her.

Article Title: With 45 mandals, Kamathipura is Mumbai's largest Ganeshotsav cluster
Article Text:
In photo: Bappa Barfani of Lane 8 Kamathipura is a popular idol on social media, Mumbai Cha Ganadhyaksh, Mumbai Cha Chintamani

The erstwhile red light district has long since gentrified. What remains is an upwardly mobile locality of 3rd generation youth striving to promote their century-old Ganeshotsav traditions.





A well-kept secret of Mumbai’s Ganeshotsav is the treasure trove of grand Ganpati idols located in Kamathipura in South Mumbai. The former red-light district has 45 Ganesh mandals, some 80-100 years old, sprinkled across 16 cross lanes. Each idol is just two minutes away. Most commercial sex workers (CSWs) are long gone. However, the past reputation of the locality precedes it. Funds are scarce. Footfall is lower than Lalbaug-Parel and Khetwadi despite the fact that there are more moortis in the Kamathipura cluster. CSWs cannot go out and seek donations because people ridicule them. Yet, stoically, the third generation of the locality continues its Ganeshotsav tradition.These young men in their 30s are well-educated, well-spoken, practising chartered accountants, doctors and engineers. They are trying hard to extricate Kamathipura from its image by inviting Mumbaikars to see their Ganeshotsav celebrations. Women make reels at midnight and post them on Instagram to impress how beautiful and safe Ganeshotsav in Kamathipura is.Anil Lakkabathini, who heads the Mumbai Cha Ganadhyaksh of 10th Lane, explains that Kamathipura was named after the kamathis (labourers) from Telangana and Andhra Pradesh who migrated after 1795 and constructed Mumbai’s fabled structures like CSMT, BMC, Bombay High Court and Rajabai Tower.“In the late 19th and early 20th centuries it became known as the city’s red-light district although traders lived here too. Today a new generation of educated residents is employed in business, banking, finance and govt sectors.”The 81-year-old Ganadhyaksh is a magnificent 22-ft Vishnu Avatar idol. All members are well qualified — Lakkabathini himself is a chartered accountant.In fact, a few Ganesh mandals have removed Kamathipura from their names. Filmmaker Dhaval Pitale of the 77-year-old Mumbaicha Ganadhisha, 11th Lane, says CSWs are now limited to just three lanes 11-13.“Our mandal is in the heart of the red-light area in Lane 11. We are at pains to explain that all of Kamathipura is not a den. In fact, CSWs and transgender persons actively help our Aadishakti mandal.”The 22-ft ‘baal swaroop’ Ganadhisha stands upon a lotus held in an elephant’s trunk. The 15-ft-tall Kamathipura Cha Krupalu of Lane 7 has been drawing crowds.Secretary Aatish Patil says, “Many people are reluctant to visit Kamathipura because of the old misconception. But it is a very safe area. One can roam freely at night also. The commercial sex workers are unobtrusive—they even confine themselves indoors if police ask them to.”Social media has high praise for Bappa Barfani of Lane 8, whose 33-ft Natraj-style Ganesh has five snakes wrapped around its body.Media in-charge Shriram Nair says the third generation helms the 72-year-old mandal.“They are IAS officers, bankers and graphic artists. I am a doctor. Our mandal is trying hard to extricate CSWs from the world’s oldest profession. Twelve have succeeded within the past year. All women perform seva and contribute to Ganeshotsav by bringing modaks and naivedya plates. We instil awareness about sexual health, try to find them jobs, arrange health camps. But Kamathipura is an area no corporate would like to enter. ”Vice-president Aniket Hiramani says, “Kamathipura gets its name from the labour class. Our redevelopment plan may launch around Diwali.”Some are afraid this will be their last Ganeshotsav.
Article Summary: Kamathipura in South Mumbai is a well-kept secret of Mumbai’s Ganeshotsav. The former red-light district has 45 Ganesh mandals, some 80-100 years old, sprinkled across 16 cross lanes. Most commercial sex workers (CSWs) are long gone.

Esteemed artists like Hariharan and cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar mingled with emerging vocalists. MUSIC, DEVOTION AND BAPPA





At Shankar Mahadevan 's SaSha Villa, Ganpati celebrations are as much about music and togetherness as they are about devotion. This year’s Bhajan Sandhya, that is one of the special evenings of the 11-day festival, once again brought the music fraternity together for an evening that began with a divine aarti and gradually turned into a spirited, night-long celebration of music, friendship and faith.The evening saw singers, musicians, performers and friends come together to seek Bappa’s blessings and celebrate through music. Among those present were Hariharan, Shaan, Mahalakshmi Iyer, Richa Sharma, Mame Khan, Pratibha Singh Baghel, Ojas Adhiya, Sivamani, Rakesh Chaurasia, Purbayan Chatterjee, Priyanka Barwe, Antara Nandy, Ankita Nandy and many others. Cricketing legend Sachin Tendulkar attended the celebrations with wife Anjali and daughter Sara, while actor Shabana Azmi and lyricist Javed Akhtar were also part of the gathering.What makes the SaSha Villa Bhajan Sandhya special is the spontaneity of the evening. Rather than being a conventional concert, it becomes a musical coming together, with artistes taking the stage, joining one another and creating music in the moment.This year, several of the singers and musicians in attendance also performed, turning the evening into an ever-evolving musical jam.Shankar Mahadevan himself took the stage, while his sons Siddharth Mahadevan and Shivam Mahadevan performed, making it a special family celebration. Percussionist Sivamani, sitar player Purbayan Chatterjee, tabla player Ojas Adhiya added their musical energy to the night, while singers across genres brought their own styles to the gathering.Javed Akhtar added another dimension to the evening when he took the stage to recite poetry, bringing the world of words and music together in the intimate setting. One of the youngest singers to perform was Nivedita Padmanabhan who sang her song from Hanuman Ansh.For Shankar and his family, the Bhajan Sandhya has become an annual tradition that brings together their extended musical family. Earlier editions of the celebration have similarly seen leading singers and musicians gather at SaSha Villa for a night of devotional music and spontaneous collaborations. Shankar says, "Our Bhajan Sandhya is a beautiful eveing of Ganpati celebration. It is a coming together of various artistes to perform here as seva for Bappa. "At the centre of it all was Shankar, who performed alongside the younger generation of the Mahadevan family. Siddharth and Shivam’s presence on stage added to the sense of the evening being a celebration not just of Ganpati, but also of the family’s shared love for music.And holding it all together was Sangeeta Mahadevan, who played the perfect hostess, welcoming guests and making the sprawling celebration feel like an intimate gathering of friends and family.(L-R)(Top:)Among the youngest singers to perform that night was Nivedita Padmanabhan,who brought a devotional touch to the evening with her song Raam Bhajan Ki Or from the superhit 'Hanuman Ansh'. Her performance was another reminder of the way Shanakr Mahadevan brings together artistes across generations and has established names sharing the same stage with younger voices.By the time the night progressed into the early hours, the gathering had become less a formal event and more a celebration of music in its purest form. From devotional melodies and familiar songs to instrumental exchanges, poetry and spontaneous performances, the evening reflected the spirit that has come to define the Mahadevan family’s Ganpati celebrations. At SaSha Villa, the music may change every year, the artistes may vary, and new voices may join the celebration, but the essence remains the same — Bappa bringing musicians, performers, friends and family together under one roof for a night of music, devotion and joy.
Article Summary: Shankar Mahadevan's SaSha Villa was transformed into a divine space during the Bhajan Sandhya for Ganpati celebrations. Article Title: Five mild-intensity earthquakes recorded around Koyna dam in Satara district
Article Text:
Kolhapur:





Five mild-intensity earthquakes measuring between 2.1 and 2.5 on the Richter scale between 12.30am and 4.30am on Tuesday were recorded in the vicinity of Koyna dam in Patan tehsil of Satara district.The region falls in a seismically active zone, and therefore multiple earthquakes occur in the region. However, most of the earthquakes are not felt, and there is damage caused to the properties. Tremors that are above 3.0 on the Richter scale are normally felt.The first quake was recorded at 12.30am on a scale of 2.1, followed by the second quake- an hour later at a scale of 2.3. The third quake occurred at 3.15am on a scale of 2.5, then at 3.30am, a scale of 2.1 was recorded. The final quake struck at 4.30am at a magnitude of 2.1, with the epicentres located around 48 to 52km from Satara city. These quakes were reported by Satara's earthquake recording station.The earthquake recording station at Koyna dam is currently non-operational, due to which the depth of the epicentre, the longitudes and latitudes could not be ascertained. Earthquake recording and measurement devices are installed at Warna dam as well. Data from three centres: Koyna, Warna and Satara was used to get more details on the quakes.
Article Summary: Five mild-intensity earthquakes measuring between 2.1 and 2.5 on the Richter scale were recorded in the vicinity of Koyna dam in Patan tehsil of Satara district. The region falls in a seismically active zone, and therefore multiple earthquakes occur in the region.

Article Title: LPG leak triggers blast at Sanpada snacks shop in Navi Mumbai, 2 injured
Article Text:
A LPG cylinder leakage caused a blast at a Sanpada snacks shop on Tuesday morning.





NAVI MUMBAI: Two men sustained severe burn injuries after a LPG cylinder leakage triggered a blast at a snacks shop on the ground floor of a society in sector-1, Sanpada on Tuesday morning. The impact of the blast was so severe that the glass facade of a hospital, located about 50 feet away, was shattered. Fortunately, the patients and staff at the hospital were not hurt.Purushottam Jadhav, Divisional officer of Vashi fire station said, "At 6.13 am, the Vashi fire station received the emergency call informing about a cylinder blast at a snacks shop in Pratik CHS on sector-1, Sanpada. The fire bridge team reached the spot within 5 minutes.It was found that the blast was due to leakage in one of the three LPG cylinders kept at snacks shop. The two men working at the snacks shop sustained severe burn injuries and were rushed to NMMC hospital, Vashi. Those injured were identified as Arjun Yadav (46) who has sustained 75 precent burn injuries and Manish Yadav (26), who has sustained 90 percent burns.The blast even caused damage to two shops adjacent to the snacks shop and three other shops in the neighbouring Abhimanyu CHS. While, the glass facade of Suraj hospital located opposite to Pratik CHS was shattered due to the impact of the blast."
Article Summary: Two men sustained severe burn injuries after a LPG cylinder leakage triggered a blast at a snacks shop on the ground floor of a society in Sanpada. The impact of the blast was so severe that the glass facade of a hospital, located about 50 feet away, was shattered. Fortunately, the patients and staff at the hospital were not hurt.

Article Title: Khalapur temple theft: Video shows masked man stealing silver Padukas; 2 arrested in Pune
Article Text:
he accused stole silver Charan Paduka from Shree Swami Samarth temple on September 2





NAVI MUMBAI: The Khalapur police probing the theft case wherein a masked man had decamped with a pair of silver toe-knob sandals (Charan Paduka) representing divine footprints offered at Shree Swami Samarth temple in Khalapur city on September 2, have arrested the acccused thief and his aide by tracking them to Pune on Monday.Pradeep Rayannavar, senior inspector of Khalapur informed that, the arrested accused are Mahendrasingh Rathod, 45, who hails from Rajasthan and Ravi Soni, 32, who hails from UP and is a history-sheeter as a theft case is registered against him in Pune.Both were presently residing in Chikhali, Pune district.On September 2, the temple trustee Deepak Bodarde, 68, lodged a complaint of theft of silver Padukas from the temple.When the CCTV footage of the temple premises was checked, it was seen that a masked man wearing a hat and attired in white Kurta-Payjama entering the temple around 7.30am.He goes to the first floor of the temple where the silver Padukas were kept in front of the idol of Shree Swami Samarth.By pretending to offer prayers, he picked up the Padukas and hid them inside his Kurta and exited the temple.Inspector Rayannavar said," The theft was committed when the temple priest had gone to his room near the temple.Upon checking the CCTV footage of the roads near the temple, it was seen that two masked men on a bike were loitering near the temple and conducted a reece before committing the theft.""Considering the religious sentiments of the devotees, Raigad SP forms a special police team to detect the case at the earliest. Subsequently, the CCTV footage along the escape route of the thieves were scanned. The bike used in the crime did not have a registration number plate," Rayannavar added.He further said, "However, using technical expertise, intelligence inputs and footages of CCTV camera along the highways, the thieves on bike were tracked and apprehended from Chikhali in Pune district. We have seized from them the stolen Padukas and the bike used in the crime. On Monday, the acccused were produced before the Khalapur JMFC court that remanded them to police custody till Friday."
Article Summary: A pair of silver toe-knob sandals (Charan Paduka) representing divine footprints offered at Shree Swami Samarth temple in Khalapur city were stolen on September 2. The accused thief and his aide were arrested by tracking them to Pune on Monday.

Article Title: Cop dies by suicide at Navi Mumbai lodge, names ex-DCP, ACP and head clerk in note alleging harassment
Article Text:
The deceased identified as Pandurang Nimba Patil, a resident of Airoli.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 55-year-old Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) with the Navi Mumbai Police allegedly died by suicide at a lodge in Airoli on Saturday evening.The deceased, identified as Pandurang Nimba Patil, a resident of Airoli, had recorded a video before taking the drastic step and posted it on social media.In the video, he alleged that he was compelled to end his life due to harassment by a former DCP, an ACP, and a head clerk.ASI Patil also left behind a nine-page suicide note accusing former DCP (Headquarters) Sanjay Patil, ACP Girish Thakare, and administrative head clerk Jayu Ahire of driving him to take the extreme step by allegedly harassing him while assigning official duties.ACP (Rabale Division) Rahul Dhas said, "ASI Patil had checked into Sachi Lodging and Boarding on Saturday at 4.40 pm. Around 7.30 pm, when the housekeeping staff went to his room, he did not respond, and the door was locked from inside. The lodge manager opened the door with a master key and found ASI Patil hanging from a ceiling fan hook. The lodge manager informed the Rabale MIDC police. ASI Patil was rushed to NMMC Hospital in Vashi, where he was declared brought dead. Prima facie, an accidental death case will be registered at the Rabale MIDC police station."
Article Summary: Pandurang Nimba Patil, a 55-year-old Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) with the Navi Mumbai Police, allegedly died by suicide at a lodge in Airoli on Saturday evening. He recorded a video before taking the drastic step and posted it on social media. In the video, he alleged that he was compelled to end his life due to harassment by a former DCP, an ACP, and a head clerk.

Article Title: 12-year-old girl, young woman rescued from prostitution racket in Navi Mumbai
Article Text:
Cops can be seen walking with 2 women. (AI-generated image used for representational purpose)





NAVI MUMBAI: The Anti-Human Trafficking Unit (AHTU) of Navi Mumbai crime branch rescued a 12-year-old girl and a 26-year-old woman from a prostitution racket being carried out at a lodge in Nerul after conducting a raid by sending a decoy customer on Thursday.The police have arrested two managers of the lodge and a waiter for allegedly supplying women for prostitution to customers by providing them rooms at Kohinoor Palace Lodging and Boarding in Shiravane village, Nerul.Gajanan Kadam, AHTU senior inspector, said the rescued minor girl hails from UP and resided in Shiravane village with her cousins, who had brought her from UP after telling her parents that she would be given a job.The trap was laid after receiving a tip-off about prostitution being carried out at the lodge. A decoy customer was sent to the lodge, where he demanded a woman for sexual favours after booking a room. The accused demanded Rs 4,000 for supplying a woman.After the accused accepted the amount, the decoy customer signalled the police team waiting outside the lodge, following which they raided the premises.Inspector Kadam said, “The arrested accused are the lodge managers identified as Hridaykumar Singh and Deepak Ramrakhiani and the waiter Kuleshwar Kumar Singh.”At Nerul police station, an FIR was registered against the arrested accused by invoking BNS sections for trafficking of persons and joint criminal liability, along with the POCSO Act, which defines punishment for abetment, such as helping, encouraging or plotting any sexual crime against a child, and the Prevention of Immoral Traffic Act.On Friday, the three accused were produced before the Belapur JMFC court, which remanded them to police custody till Sept 9.
Article Summary: The police have arrested two managers of the lodge and a waiter for allegedly supplying women for prostitution to customers. The trap was laid after receiving a tip-off about prostitution being carried out at the lodge. A decoy customer was sent to the lodge, where he demanded a woman for sexual favours.

Article Title: Mahrashtra TET paper leak: 3,470-page chargesheet details heist
Article Text:
(Photo credit:ANI) Maharashtra TET (Teacher Eligibility Test) paper leak main accused Bijendra Kumar Gupta and his associate Indrajit Singh alias Piku were brought to Bhiwandi in Thane





BHIWANDI: The Special Investigation Team has filed a 3,470-page chargesheet in the Maharashtra Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) paper leak case before the Bhiwandi Magistrate Court.The document names 18 accused detailing the roles of 16 arrested individuals and two absconding suspects, in an interstate racket that breached confidential security protocols to smuggle question papers out of the printing press from Agra.The chargesheet outlines the complete paper trail, money transactions, and recovery of the four original sets of question papers from the alleged kingpin, Bijen-dra Gupta, who was arrested from Bihar following an extensive interstate manhunt.According to the chargesheet, the breach originated at Mahim Patran Pvt Ltd in Agra contracted to print the examination sheets.Defective question sheets bearing minor ink blemishes or printing misalignments were routinely discarded into an on-site disposal bin before destruction. Taking advantage of the absence of CCTV surveillance, two press workers managed to retrieve the rejected papers
Article Summary: The Special Investigation Team has filed a 3,470-page chargesheet in the Maharashtra Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) paper leak case before the Bhiwandi Magistrate Court. The document names 18 accused detailing the roles of 16 arrested individuals and two absconding suspects.
